Helen and I collaborate daily on cross-functional initiatives at Lumina Games, where she leads product strategy for our mobile-first titles. Our interactions revolve around aligning creative vision with technical feasibility, often in high-pressure timelines. She’s the go-to person when priorities shift, and her calm demeanor keeps the team grounded.  

Helen’s day-to-day work centers on balancing stakeholder demands without losing sight of the player experience. I’ve watched her navigate complex roadmap decisions, like pivoting a flagship game’s monetization model mid-cycle based on real-time feedback. Her ability to prioritize tasks while maintaining clear communication across design, engineering, and marketing is impressive. She also mentors junior PMs, sharing frameworks for tracking progress without overcomplicating workflows.  

A standout moment came when she spearheaded a last-minute feature rollout for a launch event. By reorganizing the sprint backlog and rallying the team around a shared goal, she delivered a polished result under tight deadlines. Another instance was resolving a conflict between creative and technical teams over a core mechanic—she facilitated a compromise that preserved both innovation and feasibility.  

Helen’s strength lies in her adaptability and knack for turning ambiguity into actionable steps. She’s a reliable collaborator who consistently elevates the team’s output without seeking recognition. If you’re looking for someone who thrives in dynamic environments and drives results through clarity and teamwork, Helen is an excellent fit.
